Print an object for debugging

Source: R/debug-print.R
debug_print.Rd

Prints an object's expression, the call stack from which debug_print is called, and the evaluated result of the expression. The whole thing is surrounded by horizontal lines. This may be useful for simple debugging.

Usage

debug_print(x, note = NULL)

Arguments

x

An object to print.

note

An optional string (or something coercible to a string) to be printed. Useful for giving more context.

Value

Invisibly returns x.

Examples

# inspect `x` inside a function
my_sum <- function(x) {
  debug_print(x)
  sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

my_sum(1:5)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾

# inspect `x_i` inside a nested function
sum_of_means <- function(...) {
  sum(
    sapply(list(...), \(x_i) {
      debug_print(x_i)
      mean(x_i)
    }),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}

sum_of_means(1:3, 4:6)
